Excel-saved Power Pivot workbook (M11.33, docs/gaps.md G100)
============================================================

What: excel-model.xlsx, a workbook Microsoft Excel saved with a data model built from our own
synthetic worksheet tables: Product (5 rows), Customer (3 rows), Sales (12 rows, a date
column), two relationships Sales -> Product and Sales -> Customer, three measures
(Total quantity with a whole-number format and a description, Revenue with a two-decimal
format, Customers with the General format). Every name and value is invented; no Microsoft
asset, no client data.

Made with: Microsoft Excel 16.0, build 16.0.20625.20108 (Microsoft 365, Windows 11), on
2026-11-23, by make-model.ps1 (this folder) through Excel's public COM object model
(Workbook.Connections.Add2 with CreateModelConnection, Model.ModelRelationships.Add,
Model.ModelMeasures.Add, Workbook.RemovePersonalInformation; Excel VBA reference on Microsoft
Learn):

    powershell -File make-model.ps1 -OutPath <dir>\excel-model.xlsx -TempDir <neutral-dir>

The script starts its own Excel with TEMP set to <neutral-dir>, a short folder named after no
user, which the data model backup records as the engine's working folder. Excel also records the computer name in
the backup's PARTITIONS file; it was replaced, at the same length, by

    cargo run -p bicraft-powerpivot --example scrub_workbook -- <in> <out> <COMPUTERNAME>=<same-length text>

which rewrites only that uncompressed file and its CRC end marker, rewrites the ZIP container
(same parts, same content), and checks that the name is found nowhere else. Excel 16.0.20625
opened the scrubbed file and loaded its model (check-model.ps1, this folder).

Excel's own results: check-model.ps1 prints the model as Excel's object model lists it and
evaluates three DAX queries in Excel's engine:

    ROW: Total quantity 58, Revenue 263.96, Customers 3
    by Customer[Country]: France 217.73 / 31, Belgium 46.23 / 27
    by Product[Category]: Tools 132.5 / 40, Toys 51.5 / 14, Home 79.96 / 4

The engine test `a_workbook_excel_saved_opens_with_excels_results_and_saves_as_pbix`
(crates/engine/src/workbook_import_tests.rs) expects these values from BIcraft's evaluator;
crates/powerpivot/tests/excel_saved.rs checks the model, every value and every CRC marker.

Not covered: Excel's object model has no call to add a calculated column, a hierarchy, a
display folder or a hidden column, so the workbook has none.
